title: Fibrewise flatness test retained after arbitrary parameter base change
statement: Let $S,X,Y$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $p:X\to S$, $q:Y\to S$, $f:X\to Y$ satisfy $q\circ f=p$. Assume $p$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and $q$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For $x\in X$ and $s=p(x)$, write $f_s:X_s\to Y_s$ for the induced map of scheme-theoretic fibres [def-pc-scheme-fibre, def-pc-fibre-product], and $\widetilde x\in X_s$ for the unique point mapping to $x$. Then $f$ is flat at $x$ if and only if $f_s$ is flat at $\widetilde x$. Furthermore, for every scheme $T$ and morphism $h:T\to S$, put $X_T=X\times_ST$, $Y_T=Y\times_ST$ and let $p_T:X_T\to T$, $q_T:Y_T\to T$ be the projections and $f_T:X_T\to Y_T$ the induced map. The morphism $p_T$ is flat and locally of finite presentation, and $q_T$ is locally of finite type. For every $x'\in X_T$, putting $t=p_T(x')$ and taking its unique point $\widetilde{x'}\in(X_T)_t$, one has $f_T\text{ flat at }x'\iff(f_T)_t\text{ flat at }\widetilde{x'}$. No finiteness or flatness assumption on $h$ or $T$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 05VJ, lemma-base-change-criterion-flatness-fibre, proof from the fibrewise description of U through the sentence that the hypotheses remain in force after base change; Tag 039C, theorem-criterion-flatness-fibre, structure-sheaf specialization, together with pointwise flat ascent.

proof.text: Fix $x$, set $y=f(x)$ and $s=p(x)$. Write $i_X:X_s\to X$ and $i_Y:Y_s\to Y$ for the fibre projections. The square with horizontal maps $i_X,i_Y$ and vertical maps $f_s,f$ is cartesian: maps from a scheme $Z$ to its upper-left corner are precisely pairs $a:Z\to X$, $b:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ with $pa=sb$; adding the map to $Y$ forces it to be $fa$ since $qf=p$. This is also the universal property of $X\times_Y Y_s$. The fibre homeomorphism gives the unique points $\widetilde x,\widetilde y$ over $x,y$, and commutativity and uniqueness give $f_s(\widetilde x)=\widetilde y$.

source.place: Tags 01K0, schemes-definition-fibre, and 01K1, schemes-lemma-fibre-topological; universal property of fibre products, Tag 001V.

proof.text: If $f$ is flat at $x$, apply clause (1) of the pointwise base-change lemma to $f$, the map $i_Y:Y_s\to Y$, and the point $\widetilde x$ in the cartesian square of step 1. It gives flatness of $f_s$ at $\widetilde x$. In particular this implication does not require $i_Y$ to be flat.

Conversely suppose $f_s$ is flat at $\widetilde x$. Since $p$ is flat, its definition gives flatness at $x$. Apply the fibrewise-flatness criterion to $S,X,Y,p,q,f,x$: $p$ is locally of finite presentation, $q$ is locally of finite type, and its two pointwise flatness hypotheses have just been verified. It gives both flatness of $f$ at $x$ and flatness of $q$ at $y$; retain the first conclusion. Together with step 2 this proves the claimed equivalence.

source.place: Tag 039C, more-morphisms-theorem-criterion-flatness-fibre (1) implies (2), structure-sheaf case; fibrewise description in Tag 05VJ.

proof.text: Let $h:T\to S$ be arbitrary. Base-change stability of flat morphisms gives $p_T$ flat. Clause (3) of the qcqs-morphism-permanence lemma, specifically its locally-of-finite-presentation assertion, gives $p_T$ locally of finite presentation. Base-change stability of locally finite type morphisms gives $q_T$ locally of finite type. Each result permits every scheme morphism $h$, so no flatness, finiteness, quasi-compactness or Noetherian assumption on $h$ or $T$ has been introduced.

The defining projection equations for $f_T$ give $q_Tf_T=p_T$. Fix $x\prime\in X_T$ and put $t=p_T(x\prime)$. Repeat steps 1--3 with $(S,X,Y,p,q,f,x)$ replaced by $(T,X_T,Y_T,p_T,q_T,f_T,x\prime)$. Step 4 verifies all their hypotheses. Thus $f_T$ is flat at $x\prime$ if and only if $(f_T)_t$ is flat at its unique fibre point over $x\prime$, as required.
